perception_hz.source: label-free: 1 / median interval between battle frames

miss_isolated.source: labels, tracker output: labelled units with no deploy / spell flag and no labelled unit within overlap_radius that the tracker did not report

miss_deploy.source: labels, tracker output: missed share of units flagged `deploy`
miss_deploy.note: includes units not yet confirmed (the first-seen delay)

miss_overlap.source: labels, tracker output: missed share of units with another labelled unit within overlap_radius cells

miss_spell.source: labels, tracker output: missed share of units flagged `spell`

miss_mean_frames.source: label-free: mean run of frames a confirmed track has no box (within a track + stitched re-acquisitions)
miss_mean_frames.note: within a track only: 1.63 over 2301 runs (cannot exceed 4 frames, the tracker's memory); geometric fit for that cut-off 1.78. Misses at the start or end of a unit's life are not runs here.

first_seen_delay_frames.source: label-free: frames from a new track's first box (>= the tracker floor) to the first frame it is emitted; 16 evenly spaced order statistics
first_seen_delay_frames.note: mean 0.39 frames, 0.728 of new units emitted at once. A lower bound: frames before the detector's first box need labelled bursts. The default miss_deploy already contains this delay, so with both set the first frames are slightly over-hidden

spurious_per_unit.source: labels, tracker output: false boxes that are not ghost-like, per correctly reported unit
spurious_per_unit.note: all false boxes per reported unit: 0.069; ghost-like (left on a dead unit): 0.019, which the model draws separately (ghost_death_prob)

spurious_frames.source: labels, tracker output: frames the false box's track was shown in the replay, 16 order statistics weighted by 1/length (a labelled frame catches a long false track more often than a short one; the model draws one duration per spurious box)
spurious_frames.note: as caught on the labelled frames, unweighted: [1, 1, 1, 3, 9, 17, 32, 80]; mean per false track 2.28 frames. A long-lived false track is a persistent misreading (or a real unit the labels do not have), not a flicker; 16 entries cannot carry that rare long tail, so the model's false boxes are shorter and more numerous than the real ones

spurious_near_unit.source: labels, tracker output: share of those false boxes within 1.5 tiles of a labelled unit

wrong_side.source: labels, tracker output: reported units (side certain) on the wrong side

wrong_side_lifelong.source: labels, tracker output: share of wrong-side units whose track showed that side on >= 90% of its frames
wrong_side_lifelong.why: only 27 samples (< 30); measured value kept for reference

wrong_card_form.source: labels, tracker output: wrong form, among reported units whose card has another form

wrong_card_lookalike.source: labels, tracker output: read as its lookalike, among reported units whose card has one

wrong_card_other.source: labels, tracker output: read as another card

wrong_card_lifelong.source: labels, tracker output: share of wrong-card units whose track showed that card on >= 90% of its frames

flip_mean_frames.source: label-free: mean run of frames the tracker's emitted side or base class differs from the track's final vote
flip_mean_frames.note: 602 of 748 runs start on the track's first emitted frame (wrong at first, corrected by the vote); the model starts transient errors at any time

pos_bias_sigma.source: labels, tracker output: the default error shape scaled by 1.078 so its median radial error is the measured 0.322 tiles
pos_bias_sigma.note: the split into per-unit bias, per-frame jitter and tail is the default's, not measured (measured p95 0.868, same cell 0.585)

pos_jitter_sigma.source: labels, tracker output: the default error shape scaled by 1.078 so its median radial error is the measured 0.322 tiles
pos_jitter_sigma.note: the split into per-unit bias, per-frame jitter and tail is the default's, not measured (measured p95 0.868, same cell 0.585)

pos_tail_sigma.source: labels, tracker output: the default error shape scaled by 1.078 so its median radial error is the measured 0.322 tiles
pos_tail_sigma.note: the split into per-unit bias, per-frame jitter and tail is the default's, not measured (measured p95 0.868, same cell 0.585)

label_free_reference.note: lower bounds from the frame sequence alone; shown for comparison, not written to the config

cannot_see: A unit the detector never fires on (no box at the tracker floor on any frame): it has no track, so it is in none of these numbers.
The frames a unit is on screen before its first box and after its last box: a miss at either end of a unit's life is not a gap here. Every miss rate above is therefore a LOWER bound.

A miss longer than the tracker's memory (4 frames here): the track is dropped and the unit comes back as a new track. Those are only recovered by the stitching rule, which can also join two different units of one class (a Skeleton that died next to one that spawned).
A class or side error that lasts the unit's whole life: the reference is the track's own final vote, so a unit that is always read wrong agrees with itself. Only transient errors show up here.
Whether a short-lived or never-confirmed track was a false box or a real unit that died at once.
Position error (there is no true position without labels).
